attrs.label: Every type of Google Ads campaign
attrs.html:
Every type of Google Ads campaign

Pick a campaign type to see how we run it, the problems we fix, the best practices we follow and what it looks like.

Search campaigns

Search campaigns put a text ad at the top of Google at the moment someone searches for what you sell. It’s usually the most profitable part of an account, because the buyer has already told Google what they want. Our method starts with intent, not volume: we group keywords by what the searcher is trying to do, from early research (“best invoice software”) to ready to buy (“invoice software pricing”).

Brand, competitor and generic searches each get their own campaign and budget, so cheap brand clicks never hide expensive generic ones. Every ad group gets ads written for that intent and a landing page that answers the search. Then we let the data decide: bids follow conversions you can trust, and budget moves to the searches that turn into customers.

What we set up

  • Keyword research from your sales calls, Search Console and competitor gaps
  • Separate campaigns for brand, competitor and generic searches
  • Responsive search ads with up to 15 headlines, pinned where it matters
  • Sitelinks, callouts, prices, images and lead forms on every ad

Common problems we find

  • Broad match switched on with no negative keywords
  • Brand and generic searches mixed in one campaign
  • Every ad sending people to the homepage
  • Smart bidding learning from broken conversion tracking

How we optimise

  • Search terms reviewed every week, and the waste excluded
  • Target CPA or ROAS bidding once there are enough conversions
  • Ad tests run one change at a time
  • Budget moved weekly to the lowest cost per qualified lead

Best practices we follow

  • Conversion tracking tested before any spend
  • Shared negative keyword lists across the account
  • Ad schedules and locations matched to when and where you sell
  • Every change logged, so you can see what we did and why

Performance Max

Performance Max is one campaign that runs across Search, YouTube, Display, Discover, Gmail and Maps. Google’s automation decides where each ad appears and how much to bid. That makes it powerful, and also easy to waste money with, because it chases whatever you tell it counts as success.

Our approach is to control the inputs. We give it accurate conversion values, separate asset groups for each product line or audience, strong images and video, and audience signals from your customer lists. We exclude your brand so it can’t claim credit for people already looking for you, and we check where the money really goes every week.

What we set up

  • Asset groups by product line or audience
  • Images, video and headlines made for each asset group
  • Audience signals from customer lists and site visitors
  • Brand exclusions and URL rules set from day one

Common problems we find

  • Most of the budget spent on your own brand searches
  • One asset group for everything you sell
  • Auto-generated videos that look cheap
  • Optimising for low-value actions like page views

How we optimise

  • Search and channel insights reviewed every week
  • Weak images, videos and headlines replaced every month
  • Conversion values adjusted so it chases profitable sales
  • New-customer goals where repeat buyers dominate

Best practices we follow

  • A standard brand search campaign runs alongside it
  • Four to six weeks of data before judging it
  • Real conversion values, not just conversion counts
  • Never launched on tracking we haven’t tested

Display and Demand Gen

Display and Demand Gen campaigns show image and video ads across YouTube, Discover, Gmail and millions of partner websites and apps. They reach people before they search, so they’re the cheapest way to get your name in front of the right audience, and to bring back people who visited.

The risk is paying for accidental clicks in mobile games and low-quality sites. We start narrow: audiences built from your customers, people who searched for your category and visitors to your site. Creative is designed in-house for every size, placements are checked every week, and we judge results on leads and assisted sales, not cheap impressions.

What we set up

  • Banner and feed creative in every size, designed in-house
  • Lookalike and custom search audiences
  • Separate prospecting and remarketing campaigns
  • Frequency caps and placement exclusions set at launch

Common problems we find

  • Budget spent in mobile games and kids’ apps
  • One generic banner for every audience
  • Judged on clicks, most of them accidental
  • The same people seeing an ad 30 times a week

How we optimise

  • Placement reports reviewed, and poor sites excluded
  • New creative every month, the weakest paused
  • Audiences narrowed or widened by cost per lead
  • Assisted conversions reported separately

Best practices we follow

  • Apps and sensitive categories excluded by default
  • Creative that matches the landing page
  • Assisted results never reported as direct sales
  • Brand safety settings checked on every campaign

Remarketing

Most people don’t enquire on their first visit. Remarketing shows ads to people who’ve already been to your site, read your pricing, watched a video or started a form, on Search, YouTube and Display, while they’re still deciding.

We build lists from what people did, not just that they visited. Someone who read your pricing page gets a different message from someone who read one blog post, and existing customers are excluded or shown upgrade offers instead. Frequency caps stop the ads from following people around for months.

What we set up

  • Lists by page, time on site and stage
  • Customer Match lists from your CRM, where you qualify
  • Different ads for pricing visitors and blog readers
  • Remarketing on Search as well as Display and YouTube

Common problems we find

  • Everyone who visited gets the same ad
  • Existing customers keep seeing sign-up ads
  • Ads following people for over a year
  • Remarketing taking credit for sales that would have happened anyway

How we optimise

  • List windows matched to your sales cycle
  • Higher search bids for high-intent lists
  • Offers and messages tested by stage
  • Results compared against people who saw no ads, where possible

Best practices we follow

  • Customers and recent converters excluded
  • A cap on how often each person sees an ad
  • Lists built only from visitors who accepted cookies
  • Short list windows for short sales cycles

Call ads and call tracking

For many businesses the best leads come by phone: clinics, law firms, trades, local services and anyone selling something people want to talk through. Call ads and call assets put a phone number or call button right in the ad, so people can ring you straight from the search results.

The hard part is knowing which calls were real. We use Google forwarding numbers on ads and on your website, count only calls long enough to be a genuine enquiry, and import booked appointments or sales from your CRM. Google then learns from conversations that made money, not wrong numbers.

What we set up

  • Call assets and call-only ads during opening hours
  • Forwarding numbers on ads and on your website
  • A minimum call length for a call to count
  • Booked appointments imported from your CRM

Common problems we find

  • Calls not tracked at all, so Google can’t learn
  • Every five-second call counted as a lead
  • Call ads running when nobody can answer
  • No link between calls and sales

How we optimise

  • Ad schedules matched to staffed hours
  • Higher bids at the times calls convert best
  • Call length threshold checked against real outcomes
  • Missed calls reported, so you can fix staffing

Best practices we follow

  • Calls from ads and from the website tracked separately
  • The same number on your ads and your site
  • What counts as a good call agreed with you
  • Call results reported by campaign and keyword

Local campaigns

Local campaigns bring people to a physical location: showrooms, clinics, branches, restaurants and service areas. Ads appear in Search and Google Maps with your address, opening hours, distance and a directions button, at the moment someone nearby is looking.

We treat each location as its own small business. Each one gets a budget, radius and ad schedule that matches how busy it is and when it’s open, and results are reported by site. Your Google Business Profile is linked and kept accurate, because a wrong phone number or opening time loses the visit.

What we set up

  • Google Business Profile linked to Google Ads
  • Location details on every search ad
  • A budget, radius and schedule for each location
  • Promoted pins on Google Maps

Common problems we find

  • One budget shared by every location
  • Ads running when the site is closed
  • Wrong hours or phone numbers on the profile
  • No idea which location the leads came from

How we optimise

  • Budget moved to the locations with capacity
  • Radius tightened or widened from distance reports
  • Calls, directions and visits tracked by site
  • Local offers tested by location

Best practices we follow

  • Business profile and ads kept in sync
  • A landing page for each location
  • Areas you don’t serve excluded
  • Results reported by location, not just in total

How we look after every account

  1. 01A specialist who knows your account

    One Google Ads specialist, not a rotating team.

  2. 02Tracking you can trust

    Every conversion tested, and matched to your CRM or store.

  3. 03New ads every month

    Written and designed in-house, and tested properly.

  4. 04Reports in leads and sales

    Cost per lead, cost per sale and return on ad spend.

attrs.title: Where your Google Ads budget leaks
attrs.lead: Most Google Ads accounts we take over waste a large share of their budget, and it rarely comes from one big mistake. It’s a handful of quiet settings and habits that cost money every day without anyone noticing. Here are the six we find most often, what they look like inside the account, and how we fix each one.

items.title: Paying for the wrong searches
items.problem: Broad match keywords pay for searches that have nothing to do with you: job seekers, students and people looking for something free.
items.fix: Weekly search term reviews, shared negative keyword lists and tighter match types, so budget goes to people who can buy.

items.title: Tracking you can’t trust
items.problem: Conversions are counted twice, or phone calls aren’t counted at all, so Google optimises towards the wrong numbers.
items.fix: Conversion tracking rebuilt and tested, with enhanced conversions and call tracking. Every action checked before we scale.

items.title: Performance Max taking credit
items.problem: Performance Max spends on people who were already searching for your brand, and reports them as new sales.
items.fix: Brand exclusions, a separate brand campaign and channel reports, so you can see what it really adds.

items.title: Every ad goes to the homepage
items.problem: People who searched for one specific thing land on a general homepage and have to hunt for it. Most leave.
items.fix: A landing page for each campaign, built and tested by our own web team, fast on phones.

items.title: Cheap leads, poor sales
items.problem: Leads look cheap in Google Ads, but sales says most of them are students, job seekers or the wrong size.
items.fix: Offline conversions from your CRM, so Google learns which leads became customers and finds more like them.

items.title: Suspensions and disapprovals
items.problem: The account was suspended, or ads keep getting disapproved, and nobody knows why.
items.fix: We find the cause, fix the website and policy issues, and prepare the appeal. Google makes the final decision.

How we run your Google Ads

The same clear rhythm on every account, run by people you can talk to, so you always know what’s happening and why.

  1. Week 1

    Audit and goals

    We go through your Google Ads account, tracking and landing pages, and work out what it really brings in today.

    • Wasted spend added up in dollars
    • Conversion actions checked against your CRM
    • A written audit with a 90-day plan

    Your part: A 45-minute kick-off call about your customers, margins and what a good lead is worth.

  2. Week 2

    Tracking and setup

    Conversion tracking fixed and tested, with enhanced conversions, call tracking and offline conversions from your CRM where you have one.

    • Google tag or Tag Manager set up and tested
    • Enhanced conversions and call tracking
    • GCLID captured with every lead for offline conversions
    • Looker Studio dashboard connected

    Your part: Give us access to your ad account, analytics and website tags.

  3. Weeks 3–4

    Launch

    The new campaign structure, audiences, ads and landing pages go live, with budgets agreed in writing.

    • Search, Performance Max and remarketing built to the plan
    • Responsive search ads with sitelinks, callouts and images
    • Landing pages built or improved by our web team
    • Budgets and target cost per lead agreed in writing

    Your part: Approve the ads, the pages and the budget. Nothing launches without your OK.

  4. Every week

    Optimise

    Search terms, bids, budgets, ad tests and landing page tests, every week.

    • Search terms reviewed and negatives added
    • Bids and budgets moved to what works
    • One ad or landing page test at a time
    • A short written update every Friday

    Your part: Tell us about leads that turned into customers, or didn’t.

  5. Every month

    Report and plan

    A plain-English report on leads, sales and cost per result, what we learned and what we’ll test next.

    • The plan and budget for next month

VantagePayroll

B2B softwareSearch and Performance Max · 10 months

The company
A payroll and HR software company selling to small and mid-sized businesses, with a 12-person sales team and a 30-day free trial.
The challenge
Google Ads brought plenty of form fills, but sales said most were students, job seekers and businesses too small to buy.
Why they came to us
The previous agency reported cost per lead and called it a success. Vantage wanted an agency that would measure what sales actually closed.
What they expected
Leads that sales actually wanted to call, at under $120 per sales-qualified lead, and a clear view of the pipeline Google Ads created.
What we delivered
Offline conversions from HubSpot, 2,300 irrelevant searches excluded and separate brand and generic campaigns. Google started bidding for qualified leads, not form fills.

attrs.label: How to choose a Google Ads agency
attrs.html:
How to choose a Google Ads agency

What to expect from a good agency, what to avoid, and the questions worth asking before you hand over your budget.

What you get with us

  • Ads run in your account. You own it, the data and the history
  • Conversion tracking is checked and tested before we scale spend
  • Monthly reports in leads, sales and cost per result, not just clicks
  • A named specialist who knows your account, not a rotating team
  • A written plan for the first 90 days before we start

What we never do

  • Lock you into long contracts or keep your account if you leave
  • Take a hidden cut of your ad spend
  • Report impressions and clicks as if they were results
  • Promise rankings, results or approval from the platform
  • Change budgets or targeting without telling you

Questions to ask any Google Ads agency

Ask every agency you speak to, including us. The answers tell you more than any proposal.

  1. Q1

    Who will manage my account day to day?

    Why ask: Many agencies sell with senior people and hand the work to juniors. You want to know who makes the changes, and how much experience they have.

  2. Q2

    Will the account be in my name, and do I keep it if we part ways?

    Why ask: Your account history is valuable. If the agency owns the account, you can lose years of data and learning when you leave.

  3. Q3

    How do you charge, and do you take a percentage of ad spend?

    Why ask: A percentage of spend rewards spending more, not spending well. Know exactly what you pay and what it covers.

  4. Q4

    How will you check our conversion tracking before spending more?

    Why ask: If tracking is wrong, every bid and every report is wrong too. A good agency checks it first.

  5. Q5

    What will you report on each month?

    Why ask: Clicks and impressions are easy to grow. Ask for leads, sales, cost per result and what changed.

  6. Q6

    What exactly happens in the first 90 days?

    Why ask: A clear plan shows they have looked at your account. A vague answer usually means a template.

  7. Q7

    Can you show results for a business like ours?

    Why ask: Results in your industry, or with a similar sales cycle and budget, tell you far more than a list of logos.

  8. Q8

    What is the notice period, and is there a minimum term?

    Why ask: Long lock-ins protect the agency, not you. Good agencies keep clients because of results.

attrs.title: Google Ads questions, answered
attrs.lead: Can’t find your answer? Ask us on a free 30-minute call.

items.question: What does a Google Ads agency do?
items.answer: A Google Ads agency sets up, manages and improves your campaigns: keyword research, ads, bidding, conversion tracking, landing pages and reporting. The goal is more leads and sales at a lower cost.

items.question: Is it worth hiring a Google Ads agency?
items.answer: If you spend more than a few thousand a month, usually yes. Most accounts we audit waste a fifth to a third of their budget, and fixing that alone often pays for the management fee.

items.question: Should I use Performance Max?
items.answer: Performance Max works well when tracking is solid, you have good images and video, and brand searches are excluded. Without those, it often takes credit for sales you’d have had anyway.

items.question: Are you a Google Partner agency?
items.answer: We work to Google’s best practices on every account. Ask us on the call about our current certifications.

items.question: How much does Google Ads management cost?
items.answer: We charge a fixed monthly management fee on top of your ad spend, quoted after a free call. It depends on the size of the account and the work involved. We never take a hidden cut of your Google Ads spend.

items.question: Do I keep my Google Ads account if I leave?
items.answer: Yes. Your ads run in an account you own. You keep the account, the data and all the history.

items.question: How soon will I see results?
